plan.name: real-app-hls
plan._comment: FrameConsole's browser viewing path (HLS, run with --host <sender IP>, 127.0.0.1 when the generator runs on the sender PC). Every viewer is a Node LL-HLS client: POST /screen-01/session (+ PUT heartbeat, DELETE on leave, as the page), live.m3u8, the variant of its quality, init, parts with blocking reloads, video + AAC. Quality per plan: source only here; a mix with --qualities source=0.7,720p=0.3 (the app must offer 720p). Stages 1-10-50-100-300-500-1000, hold 45 s each; on one PC the stop rules (generator threads, host CPU/memory, success, 429/503 share, degraded rate) end the run long before 1000 - that is a loopback limit, never 1,000 internet viewers. Target statistics only from the app's read-only GET /api/stats (v 1): ingest per path as the full-rate reference, hls.sessions as the target session count, http.refused. The app answers Connection: close and counts every HLS request in its 400 in-flight slots (http_server.cpp kMaxRequests), so 503 Busy answers are expected past a few hundred LL-HLS viewers. One headless Edge page with the real UI (hls.js) runs in a separate phase after the holds of stages 1 and 10: decoded fps and real delay, kept apart from the media-load numbers. Traffic cap 200 GB is loopback/LAN protection only; lower it with --max-traffic-gb on any metered link.

definitions.viewer: one Node LL-HLS client (lib/hls-client.mjs, 2 worker threads): live.m3u8 -> the variant of its quality -> init -> parts with blocking playlist reloads (_HLS_msn/_HLS_part) + the AAC rendition, viewer session with heartbeat; no decoding or rendering

hls.firstMedia: the first part/segment of every followed track (video and AAC) received completely after init; readyTime = that moment on the receiver clock
hls.delay: estimated delay = now - position of a virtual player that starts at the first unit it received (1.5 s behind the newest media, like the page liveSyncDuration), plays in real time while media is buffered, catches up at 1.1x when more than liveSync + 0.5 s is buffered, and stops at the buffer end; positions come from EXT-X-PROGRAM-DATE-TIME (the target MediaMTX clock at ingest). Needs the generator and target clocks in sync; excludes capture, encode and publish before MediaMTX, and decode/render after. The real delay is the browser sampler one (barcode / hls.js playingDate).
hls.stall: no new video part/segment for more than 3000 ms (counted when media resumes, plus one per viewer still stalled at the hold end)
hls.busy: requests answered 429 or 503 (session, live.m3u8, playlists, init, parts, segments); waits follow Retry-After (1-30 s, jitter), at most 6 in a row before the viewer restarts
hls.traffic: media bytes (init, parts, segments) of video and AAC; playlist bytes are counted separately (playlistBytesPerMediaByte)

definitions.receiving: received bytes grew by more than 0 kbit/s in a 2000 ms sample window
definitions.firstMedia: join requested (ramp slot, burst start or churn re-join; queueing included) -> the viewer's generator path has media: ready, with tracks and received bytes. The time is the path ready time (tracks gathered = first RTP) when it is a real time not before the request; MediaMTX's zero-year placeholder and earlier times are ignored. Without a usable ready time the sample clock is used and counted in firstMediaMs.basis / firstMediaFromSampleClock (error up to one sample interval).
definitions.reconnect: media again after a loss, or a new real ready time of the same session; the placeholder -> real ready time transition is not a reconnect
definitions.sustained: first media and receiving in >= 95% of the hold windows; successRate = sustained / requested
definitions.fullRate: sustained, and every quality segment the viewer watched in the hold (>= 4 s) has a mean rate >= 90% of that quality's reference (reference.<quality>.from); fullRateSuccessRate = full-rate viewers / (requested or sessions seen) minus sessions too short to judge (fullRateTooShort, all segments < minSegmentSec), not measured when a watched quality has no reference (an idle path's ingest 0 is no reference)
definitions.fullRateLive: per sample: share of viewers whose rolling 10 s rate is >= 90% of their quality's rolling reference (stop rule degraded-below-min)
definitions.stall: a 2000 ms window without growth (<= 0 kbit/s); stallTimeRatio = stalled time / observed time after first media
definitions.cpuPct: percent of the whole machine (all logical CPUs) from process CPU time; cores = same in CPU cores
definitions.unattributedCpuPct: host CPU minus generator, target and browser-sampler processes: other programs and kernel network time; a stage is flagged externalLoad when its hold mean is above 25%
definitions.rtpPacketsLost: losses reported by the generator WebRTC sources (MediaMTX log, "1 RTP packet lost" and "N RTP packets lost"); lossRatioEst assumes ~1,150 B per RTP packet
definitions.whep: WHEP signalling seen by the loopback tap (status per offer, Retry-After values); MediaMTX's WHEP client itself retries about every 5 s whatever Retry-After says
definitions.traffic: bytes received by the generator's protocol viewers (browser pages not counted)
definitions.network: generator and target location are recorded in host/target; loopback or same-PC traffic does not cross the NIC

notMeasured: decoded FPS, rendering, A/V sync, player rebuffering and live latency are not measured by protocol viewers (see browser sampler fields)
HLS: the delay estimate is not the player delay (no decode/render, MediaMTX ingest clock); RTP loss and ICE do not apply
HLS: requests the target refused are seen only as the answers the receiver got
target-side dropped frame counts: only the app count of MediaMTX "too slow, discarding" warnings (appDiscardWarnings)

trafficPlan.note: protocol viewers only (browser pages and chat not counted); per-viewer rate = the mix of the plan's qualities

delayEstimateMs.basis: sample clock - virtual playhead (EXT-X-PROGRAM-DATE-TIME of the media being played), see definitions.hls.delay

receiveDelayMs.basis: arrival of a part/segment - PROGRAM-DATE-TIME of its end

stalls.definition: no new video media for > 3000 ms

firstMediaComponentsMs.note: from the start of the viewer in the receiver (no ramp queue); firstMediaMs of the stage counts from the join request

stages.rebuffering: stall windows only (byte growth); player rebuffering not measured

definitions.firstFrameMs: page navigation start -> first presented video frame (requestVideoFrameCallback), includes page load, WHEP/ICE and first keyframe
definitions.presentedFps: presented frames per second in the window (rVFC)
definitions.latencyMs: barcode stamp (source wall clock) -> expected display time; needs a shared clock
definitions.decodedFps: WebRTC: framesDecoded delta / stats-timestamp delta of the main connection (over the window, or from its first decoded frame when made inside the window); HLS (no peer connection): getVideoPlaybackQuality totalVideoFrames delta / time (decodedFpsBasis)
definitions.pdtDelayMs: HLS (hls.js): once a second, now - hls.playingDate of the player on the shown element; the playing position by EXT-X-PROGRAM-DATE-TIME (target MediaMTX ingest clock): excludes capture/encode/publish before MediaMTX, includes buffering and decode; same clock needed
definitions.hlsLatencyMs: hls.js latency (live edge of the playlist - playing position), once a second
definitions.profiles: desktop = the window as started; mobile = DevTools emulation (390x844, DPR 3, touch, Android UA) in desktop Edge: mobile-like layout and quality choice, not a phone decoder or mobile network

pages.latencyMs: not measured (source has no live barcode)
